independent_review_record.review_notes: Medical statements were checked against ADA primary patient/professional pages. ADA states that unresolved red/white oral lesions should be reevaluated after two weeks and considered for biopsy for definitive diagnosis; MouthHealthy lists persistent sore/irritation, red/white patches, lumps, and chewing/swallowing/speaking difficulty as reasons to contact a dentist. The manuscript does not equate these signs with cancer, does not diagnose from photos, and does not prescribe a test or treatment.

official_sources.verified_facts: Any white/red oral patch that does not resolve in two weeks should be reevaluated and considered for biopsy; persistent signs merit further investigation; biopsy is the reference standard for diagnosis.

Warning signs lasting longer than two weeks include nonhealing sore/irritation, red/white patches, lump/thickening, and chewing/swallowing/speaking difficulty; a warning sign does not necessarily mean cancer.
